title.narrative: Promoting Gender Equality in and through Education in Chad

description.narrative: Most Central African countries continue to face persistent political instability, fragile security environments, and recurrent natural hazards, all of which significantly disrupt education systems. Across the region, these dynamics have intensified emerging challenges, including the rise of violent extremism, attacks on education, and entrenched gender inequalities. Chad exemplifies these compounded challenges. The country is affected by protracted insecurity linked to the Lake Chad Basin crisis, intercommunal violence, and climate-induced shocks such as droughts and floods. These overlapping crises have contributed to large-scale internal displacement, as well as a sustained influx of refugees from neighbouring countries, placing additional strain on already limited education infrastructure and resources. Across the region, and especially in Chad, these dynamics have intensified emerging challenges, including the rise of violent extremism, attacks on education, and entrenched gender inequalities. In Chad, girls remain disproportionately excluded from education due to early marriage, socio-cultural barriers, and insecurity, particularly in conflict-affected and rural areas. Schools are often under-resourced, overcrowded, or inaccessible for displaced populations, further limiting equitable access to safe and quality learning environments. Despite notable progress in recent years toward expanding access to inclusive and quality education, significant gaps remain. In Chad, disparities in access, retention, and learning outcomes are particularly pronounced among girls, refugees, internally displaced children, and children with disabilities. Addressing these inequalities is critical to ensuring the right to education without discrimination and to promoting equal opportunities for all learners. Guided by the 2026-2029 strategy on gender equality in and through education, UNESCO will engaged and support member states, especially Chad to realize their obligations and commitments to implement the right to quality inclusive education for all, and to strengthen education systems to be gender-transformative and promote gender equality. Strong collaboration will be established with other sectors, and systematic joint actions will be encouraged for improved political and financial commitment to ensure gender equality in education.
